title: Where QUERRA fits
lede: Most crop-protection technology sells a diagnosis, a map or an action. QUERRA supplies the step in between: checked field observations that an advisor can trust and that a disease forecast can be tested against.

chain.label: Forecast
chain.who: Disease-risk models and decision support, including M4

chain.label: Flag
chain.who: Satellite and drone imagery, camera traps, weather stations

chain.label: Confirm on the ground
chain.who: QUERRA: a close-range photograph, an on-device result with its uncertainty, human review and a traceable record

chainNote: The chain follows one field problem from forecast to action. Reviewed observations also flow back to the forecast; that return path is the M4 loop described above.
tableCaption: Categories, not companies: individual products differ. Checked against public information in November 2026.

categories.name: Phone diagnosis apps
categories.strong: Free or low-cost, large image libraries, many crops, an answer in seconds.
categories.stops: One photo gives one answer. Recognition usually runs on a remote server. There is no independent review step or traceable record a forecast could be tested against.
categories.relation: QUERRA works offline and keeps a review trail. It does not try to cover as many crops.

categories.name: Satellite and drone imagery
categories.strong: Whole-field coverage, repeatable, good at showing which patches differ.
categories.stops: Sees the top of the canopy. Early symptoms on lower leaves, and the cause of a patch, still need a ground check. Processing usually happens online.
categories.relation: Complementary: imagery shows where to look, QUERRA checks it on the ground.

categories.name: Camera traps and in-field sensors
categories.strong: Automatic, frequent, proven at scale for insect pests and microclimate.
categories.stops: Fixed points and specific pest groups. Most need a mobile signal.
categories.relation: Useful context next to M4. QUERRA does not replace them.

categories.name: Weeding and spraying robots
categories.strong: Large investment, commercial fleets, many hours in real fields.
categories.stops: Built to act on weeds or spray. Scouting data is a by-product.
categories.relation: QUERRA does not build carriers or sprayers. Its core is designed to ride on carriers as a payload.

categories.name: Disease-risk models and decision support
categories.strong: Regional forecasts from weather, crop stage and history. M4 is one of them.
categories.stops: They need observed ground truth to validate and recalibrate them, field by field.
categories.relation: This is the gap QUERRA is built for: reviewed observations that feed the forecast back.

apart: Works offline: inference runs on the device, so a weak connection does not stop a scouting round.
Every result carries its uncertainty and goes through human review before it counts.
Exports are fingerprinted, so anyone holding the file can check it has not changed.
Evaluation keeps related images out of the test set, and the protocol is published before the results.
Built to feed a forecast such as M4, not to compete with it.
behind: No field-validated result yet. The TRL4 evidence pack is due on 28 November 2026.
One ordinary RGB camera: no multispectral or depth sensing.
A much smaller image library than established apps.
A headline accuracy figure is not a differentiator: published wheat-disease classifiers already report over 97% on their own test sets.

carrier.title: Why we do not build the robot
carrier.body: Since 2024 a UK developer of a cereal-scouting robot has gone into liquidation, and a Danish maker of an autonomous field robot was declared bankrupt and sold in parts. Robot bases are being consolidated and are becoming commodities. QUERRA’s core is therefore designed as a payload: the evidence chain stays the same whether a person, a cart or a carrier moves it.
